subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Dark Energy: The Expanding Mystery
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Dark Energy: The Expanding Mystery.

hook.text: About 68% of the universe is dark energy—a mysterious force pushing the cosmos apart faster and faster.

buildup.text: It was discovered in 1998 when distant supernovae showed the universe's expansion is accelerating, not slowing down.

discovery.text: Nobody expected acceleration. The discovery won the Nobel Prize and remains one of the biggest surprises in modern physics.

twist.text: Dark energy might be a property of empty space—Einstein's cosmological constant, the idea he once called his greatest blunder.

climax.text: If dark energy strengthens, the universe could end in a Big Rip—tearing apart galaxies, stars, atoms, and spacetime itself.

punchline.text: Two-thirds of the universe is an unknown force. It decides the fate of everything.

quiz.question: What would happen if dark energy continues to strengthen over time?
options: It could cause a Big Rip, tearing apart galaxies, atoms, and spacetime itself
It would cause the universe to collapse back into a singularity
It would gradually convert all matter into pure energy

details.summary: Dark energy makes up about 68% of the universe's total energy and drives its accelerating expansion. Discovered in 1998 through observations of distant supernovae, its nature is completely unknown.
details.whyItMatters: Dark energy determines the ultimate fate of the universe. Understanding it would answer whether the cosmos will expand forever, freeze, or eventually rip apart — making it arguably the biggest question in physics.
takeaways: Makes up about 68% of the universe's total energy
Drives the accelerating expansion of the universe

faq.question: What is the cosmological constant?
faq.answer: Einstein originally added a cosmological constant (Λ) to his equations to keep the universe static. He later called it his biggest blunder. Today, Λ is the simplest explanation for dark energy — a constant energy density of empty space itself.

faq.question: Has dark energy always been accelerating the universe?
faq.answer: No. For the first ~8 billion years, gravity dominated and the expansion was decelerating. Around 5-6 billion years ago, dark energy's effect surpassed gravity as the universe expanded enough for matter density to dilute. Since then, expansion has been accelerating and will continue indefinitely.
